summary: Checked all 26 occurrences. L-agent Preterit and Imperativ express pushing/displacement; Detransitive tfiq/mətfəq commonly expresses autonomous encounter or finding rather than being pushed.
Targets vary between ʕal-, reciprocal bәḥḏoḏe and a zero-marked co-participant. In PrS 85/16 lu taʕlo is the pushing agent; in PrS 60/102 lu qaṭuno is likewise the agent, not the displaced patient.
Detransitive target extensions include a daughter being found, a potential rescuer, a merchant and a village. No participant-based senses are required. tfq is kept separate from wfq/wtfq agreement.

The proposed impersonal befalling sense in MAC NE Sterka Zera/29 is not established. The English parenthesis explicitly reads personal encounter and the existing SZ 5.45 text may be the same witness; retain the ambiguity as a question instead of publishing D2.

PrS 21/4, 25/5 and Talay 1/157 repeat material already represented under older references; do not add duplicate examples. The sparse active Infectum gains gtəfqinalox, with the base forms left unchanged.
MAC NE Sterka Zera/29 / SZ 5.45: is the brother subject of tfīq eba, or is the question 'what happened to her'? Collate punctuation and the two English renderings before creating an impersonal sense.
In MAC NE Habirman Xatun/18, is the second ḥa mәnne an unmarked co-participant or a dislocated subject? The clearer merchant encounter is selected for the box.
In PrS 58/67, is postposed u ǧənnawi the displaced object or an intransitive subject? The preceding shove favors the transitive analysis, retained provisionally.
Check old PrS reference concordances before changing citations; the etymology's Kurdish source remains unresolved by these occurrences.
